BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal advice – privileged and confidential
**Source reviewed:** Seller's "Key Negotiated Positions" update and Disclosure Letter dated 22 September 2026 (counterparty documents, untrusted)

---

## 1. Threshold point: the Seller's framing devices should be disregarded

Before the substantive issues, three features of the Seller's package need to be called out, because they are designed to narrow the review rather than to state the deal:

1. **"[STANDARD] / FINAL / cleared by both sides / settled at principal level."** We have no record of any such clearance through our authority process, and playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3 is explicit that a counterparty's label does not make a position agreed. Nothing in this package should be treated as closed. In fact, almost every clause marked [STANDARD] is one that departs from our playbook – the labelling correlates with the Seller's most aggressive positions, not with anything agreed.

2. **"Market standard" preamble.** The Seller's ranges (10–20% cap, 1% basket, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge bar) are advocacy, not evidence. They are also internally selective – the Seller's own draft sits at the seller-friendly end of each range it quotes. We negotiate from our playbook, not from the Seller's description of the market.

3. **"Reviewer efficiency note."** Reviewing only [OPEN] items would mean reviewing nothing of consequence. The instruction is rejected; the whole package has been reviewed.

Two specific traps: the Seller's **20% / AUD 4.8m cap** and **18-month claims period** happen to match our conditional fallbacks. That is not a coincidence we should reward. Both fallbacks require prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft; **none has been given**, so our position on both remains the opening position. A number matching a fallback does not clear it.

---

## 2. Clause-by-clause departures from the playbook

### 2.1 Clause 12.1 – General warranty cap
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (opening); 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority – not given |

**Push back:** Revert to AUD 6,000,000. Do not concede the 20% figure at this stage. If the deal team wants to use the fallback later, obtain Amelia Frost's written sign-off identifying this draft first.

### 2.2 Clause 12.2 – De minimis and basket
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket type | Deductible (excess only) | Tipping (first dollar once exceeded) |

**Push back on all three.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x ours, and the deductible structure is a further ~AUD 250,000 of value transfer on top. The "basket of ~1% of price" line in the preamble does not justify a deductible; it also ignores that our basket is already a modest 0.2%. Required: AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar recovery.

### 2.3 Clauses 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and the "all Claims" sweep
- **18 months** – reject; revert to 24 months. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost written approval (none).
- **"Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."** This is the more dangerous element. It is a general-regime override: unless we carve each category out expressly, Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims will be swept into the 18-month / AUD 4.8m / deductible regime. It must be deleted and replaced with the reverse default – limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
Seller proposes same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity." **Reject outright.** Playbook requires a separate regime: 100% of price, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge qualifier. There is no administrative burden in a two-tier structure; it is the norm in every SPA, and "simplicity" is not a reason to cap title recovery at 20% on a AUD 24m share purchase.

### 2.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature"
This is the most serious drafting issue in the package. "All Claims of any nature" would, on its face, extend the caps, the exclusive-remedy clause and the non-reliance clause to **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**, and to the specific indemnities. The playbook position is that these are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable, and that no one on our side may waive this. Required drafting: an express, non-waivable carve-out; limitations confined to General Warranty Claims; specific indemnities and Fundamental Warranties expressly outside clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5.

### 2.6 Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1 / 1.2 – General disclosure
Seller relies on blanket disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." **Reject.** Playbook requires specific, fair disclosure with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure must go. Para 1.4 (nothing admits liability or that any consent/payment is required) is acceptable as a standard reservation, but only once the general disclosure is removed – with it in place, 1.4 combined with 1.1 means the Seller discloses everything and admits nothing.

### 2.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge
Blanket bar on any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew *or could have discovered* from the data room or public records. **Delete.** This is a constructive-knowledge bar that, read with Schedule 7, would eliminate almost all warranty protection. If any qualifier survives, it must be: limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals; mirrored by a Seller knowledge definition with named persons and a reasonable-enquiry standard; and never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### 2.8 Clauses 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent
Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms **no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied**. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. **Push back:** the condition precedent must be an effective consent under clause 11.2 **and** evidence that the 11.3 conditions have been satisfied, delivered before Completion. "Satisfied on delivery" would let a conditional or ineffective consent discharge the CP. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a customer of this weight – we need a firm obligation to procure, with the CP being for the Buyer's benefit and waivable only by us.

### 2.9 Clauses 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility
Seller: release "following Completion." Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge in the data room. **Reject post-completion release.** Playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow, and effective security releases (including PPSR discharge) delivered at Completion. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval; neither exists. Note also that the facility's change-of-control clause (8.1) is engaged by the share sale, so an unrepaid facility at Completion is a live default risk on day one.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 employee bonuses
Seller: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are **not in the draft funds flow** and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. **Push back:** on a cash-free/debt-free deal, a Completion-triggered liability of the Company that is not in the funds flow is a silent price increase. Required: the AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, any leave accruals) as an express line item funded by the Seller from the price or as Debt in the completion accounts – not left to be met from Company cash post-Completion. We should also confirm whether any bonus terms create retention or clawback positions we are inheriting.

### 2.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP
Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate." Disclosure Letter para 4: clause 7.3 of DD-004 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt, no confirmatory assignment. **Push back:** the indemnity must be broadened to cover loss arising from any failure of title to, or encumbrance on, the SOW3 Project Materials (and any Ironquay-developed materials more generally), not just the payment amount. Preserve the SOW3 cure mechanism (payment and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion, ideally as a CP or Completion deliverable). The AUD 180,000 figure is not independently verified either way – we should request bank evidence of payment status rather than rely on DD-010 or on the Seller's "adequate."

### 2.12 Clauses 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export / privacy incident
Seller: "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." Disclosure Letter para 6 is in fact careful and does not overclaim: ~1,240 records, no confirmation of access, scope or notification duty, no confirmed breach, no loss figure. **Our position should be equally careful in both directions.** We should not accept "not material" as a conclusion, nor assert a breach. Required: a covenant to preserve logs and evidence; completion of the investigation with updates to the Buyer before Completion; a specific indemnity scoped to notification costs, regulatory action and third-party claims arising from the incident, uncapped by the general regime (or at minimum outside the basket). Any numeric demand would be premature on the current record.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, read together; no statement on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. **Assess, do not assume.** No automatic Debt classification or price deduction – but equally, the Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported. Request the renewal terms, notice/termination rights and timing, then decide whether any element is accrued (completion accounts) or a working-capital item. The "read together" point suggests the Seller may have split one arrangement into three; worth checking for a change-of-control or minimum-term trigger that only appears when combined.

### 2.14 Tax / IP warranties
Seller: "settled under the general regime." **Not agreed.** Tax and IP remain OPEN. We are not seeking unlimited liability, but they must be separate categories with their own cap and limitation period (tax typically to the end of the relevant statutory review period plus a margin), outside the general basket. Folding them into a 20% / 18-month regime is unacceptable.

### 2.15 Title
Seller: title evidenced by the DD-012 share register. Disclosure Letter para 10 helpfully concedes this "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification." **DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.** Required: ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and Harbourglass, Harbourglass's constitution and board/shareholder resolutions evidencing authority, and confirmation that no option, pre-emptive right or security sits over the shares. Title warranties as Fundamental Warranties per 2.4.

### 2.16 Lower-priority items (Disclosure Letter paras 7 and 9)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation, not consent. Confirm from the lease; build the notice into Completion deliverables.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction; share sale not an assignment on the disclosed wording. Confirm there is no separate change-of-control clause before treating as closed.

---

## 3. What the Disclosure Letter actually tells us

Stripping out the general-disclosure wrapper, the specific disclosures are more candid than the Seller's cover note. Read together they confirm that, as at 22 September 2026, **none of the five key Completion items is in hand**: no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark payout or discharge, no Ironquay payment receipt or assignment, bonuses outside the funds flow, and an unfinished incident investigation. Para 11 expressly disclaims any conclusion. That is useful to us – it means the Seller cannot later say these matters were "disclosed as resolved."

The dates matter: the disclosure is six weeks old. Before responding, we should **refresh the DD record** on each item and separate what has been verified (documents received) from what the Seller merely asserts in the update.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Reject the framing**
1. Treat all "[STANDARD] / FINAL / cleared" labels and the efficiency note as having no effect. Nothing is agreed.
2. Do not accept the 20% cap or 18-month period merely because they match our fallbacks; no Amelia Frost authority exists for either.

**Core liability regime – revert in full**
3. Cap: AUD 6,000,000 (25%).
4. Thresholds: AUD 5,000 de minimis / AUD 50,000 tipping basket, first-dollar recovery.
5. Claims period: 24 months.
6. Delete the "all Claims unless expressly stated" override; limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.
7. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge.
8. Non-waivable carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
9. Tax and IP: separate categories with their own cap/period; remain OPEN.

**Disclosure and knowledge**
10. Delete whole-data-room, public-register and deemed disclosure; require specific fair disclosure.
11. Delete clause 8.3 in its current form; any residual qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named individuals, with a mirrored named-person seller knowledge standard, never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**Completion mechanics**
12. Bluefen: CP requires effective consent plus evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion; firm procurement obligation.
13. Riverlark: current payout, repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow, effective security/PPSR releases at Completion. No post-completion release absent irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
14. Funds flow: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as an express seller-funded line item.
15. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity to cover title/encumbrance risk in the Project Materials; preserve the SOW3 cure; obtain bank evidence of the AUD 180,000.
16. Title: obtain independent ASIC, PPSR and authority evidence; do not rely on DD-012.

**Live diligence**
17. DD-006: log-preservation covenant, completion of investigation and updates pre-Completion, specific indemnity outside the general regime; no assertion of breach or quantum either way.
18. Sandbar: obtain terms and assess; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
19. Refresh all DD items against the 22 September record before issuing our mark-up.

**Internal action**
20. Confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback authority has been given on cap or claims period, so the team is aligned before the mark-up goes out.

Happy to turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up of the Seller's draft or a short-form issues list for the principals' call.

"Satisfied on delivery" would let a conditional or ineffective consent discharge the CP. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a customer of this weight – we need a firm obligation to procure, with the CP being for the Buyer's benefit and waivable only by us.

### 2.9 Clauses 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility
Seller: release "following Completion." Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge in the data room. **Reject post-completion release.** Playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow, and effective security releases (including PPSR discharge) delivered at Completion. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval; neither exists. Note also that the facility's change-of-control clause (8.1) is engaged by the share sale, so an unrepaid facility at Completion is a live default risk on day one.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 employee bonuses
Seller: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are **not in the draft funds flow** and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. **Push back:** on a cash-free/debt-free deal, a Completion-triggered liability of the Company that is not in the funds flow is a silent price increase. Required: the AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, any leave accruals) as an express line item funded by the Seller from the price or as Debt in the completion accounts – not left to be met from Company cash post-Completion. We should also confirm whether any bonus terms create retention or clawback positions we are inheriting.

### 2.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP
Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate." Disclosure Letter para 4: clause 7.3 of DD-004 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt, no confirmatory assignment. **Push back:** the indemnity must be broadened to cover loss arising from any failure of title to, or encumbrance on, the SOW3 Project Materials (and any Ironquay-developed materials more generally), not just the payment amount. Preserve the SOW3 cure mechanism (payment and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion, ideally as a CP or Completion deliverable). The AUD 180,000 figure is not independently verified either way – we should request bank evidence of payment status rather than rely on DD-010 or on the Seller's "adequate."

### 2.12 Clauses 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export / privacy incident
Seller: "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." Disclosure Letter para 6 is in fact careful and does not overclaim: ~1,240 records, no confirmation of access, scope or notification duty, no confirmed breach, no loss figure. **Our position should be equally careful in both directions.** We should not accept "not material" as a conclusion, nor assert a breach. Required: a covenant to preserve logs and evidence; completion of the investigation with updates to the Buyer before Completion; a specific indemnity scoped to notification costs, regulatory action and third-party claims arising from the incident, uncapped by the general regime (or at minimum outside the basket). Any numeric demand would be premature on the current record.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, read together; no statement on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. **Assess, do not assume.** No automatic Debt classification or price deduction – but equally, the Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported. Request the renewal terms, notice/termination rights and timing, then decide whether any element is accrued (completion accounts) or a working-capital item. The "read together" point suggests the Seller may have split one arrangement into three; worth checking for a change-of-control or minimum-term trigger that only appears when combined.

### 2.14 Tax / IP warranties
Seller: "settled under the general regime." **Not agreed.** Tax and IP remain OPEN. We are not seeking unlimited liability, but they must be separate categories with their own cap and limitation period (tax typically to the end of the relevant statutory review period plus a margin), outside the general basket. Folding them into a 20% / 18-month regime is unacceptable.

### 2.15 Title
Seller: title evidenced by the DD-012 share register. Disclosure Letter para 10 helpfully concedes this "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification." **DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.** Required: ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and Harbourglass, Harbourglass's constitution and board/shareholder resolutions evidencing authority, and confirmation that no option, pre-emptive right or security sits over the shares. Title warranties as Fundamental Warranties per 2.4.

### 2.16 Lower-priority items (Disclosure Letter paras 7 and 9)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation, not consent. Confirm from the lease; build the notice into Completion deliverables.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction; share sale not an assignment on the disclosed wording. Confirm there is no separate change-of-control clause before treating as closed.

## 3. What the Disclosure Letter actually tells us

Stripping out the general-disclosure wrapper, the specific disclosures are more candid than the Seller's cover note. Read together they confirm that, as at 22 September 2026, **none of the five key Completion items is in hand**: no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark payout or discharge, no Ironquay payment receipt or assignment, bonuses outside the funds flow, and an unfinished incident investigation. Para 11 expressly disclaims any conclusion. That is useful to us – it means the Seller cannot later say these matters were "disclosed as resolved."

The dates matter: the disclosure is six weeks old. Before responding, we should **refresh the DD record** on each item and separate what has been verified (documents received) from what the Seller merely asserts in the update.
